After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding its redesigned interface to iPad app users, including a new Mac-like sidebar. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app layout

Although WhatsApp began working on adjusting its iOS app to match the Liquid Glass visual overhaul as early as last October, the company only brought this redesigned interface to the iPad in June this year, conducting limited beta testing.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the redesign included Liquid Glass-styled tabs, buttons and contextual menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

According to the site's latest report, WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the bottom tab bar by default with a new Mac-like sidebar.

This sidebar follows the layout already found in the WhatsApp Mac version, providing quick access to chats, status updates, communities, calls, Meta AI and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to give more space to the chat list and conversation windows.

Here's what was reported:

WABetaInfo noted that the new sidebar has been made available to some beta testers running the latest TestFlight version, and some users on the regular App Store version have also begun seeing this change.

As is WhatsApp's usual practice, the new interface may take some time to reach all users, whether they are using beta or the official version. Nonetheless, iPad users should eventually benefit from this layout that is better suited to the tablet.
